[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "title": "Multidimensional Position, Velocity, and Acceleration Vectors",
    "scope": "Establishes vector kinematics in 2D and 3D Cartesian coordinates from fundamental definitions. Teaches the position vector, displacement between states, average velocity, and instantaneous velocity as the derivative of position along the tangent to the trajectory. Explains instantaneous acceleration as the derivative of velocity, clarifying that acceleration arises from changes in velocity magnitude, direction, or both.",
    "key_points": [
      "Position vector: $\\vec{r}(t) = x(t)\\hat{\\imath} + y(t)\\hat{\\jmath} + z(t)\\hat{k}$ and displacement $\\Delta\\vec{r} = \\vec{r}_2 - \\vec{r}_1$",
      "Average velocity: $\\vec{v}_{\\text{avg}} = \\frac{\\Delta\\vec{r}}{\\Delta t} = \\frac{\\Delta x}{\\Delta t}\\hat{\\imath} + \\frac{\\Delta y}{\\Delta t}\\hat{\\jmath} + \\frac{\\Delta z}{\\Delta t}\\hat{k}$ collinear with $\\Delta\\vec{r}$",
      "Instantaneous velocity: $\\vec{v} = \\frac{d\\vec{r}}{dt} = v_x\\hat{\\imath} + v_y\\hat{\\jmath} + v_z\\hat{k}$ is always strictly tangent to the path",
      "Instantaneous acceleration: $\\vec{a} = \\frac{d\\vec{v}}{dt} = \\frac{dv_x}{dt}\\hat{\\imath} + \\frac{dv_y}{dt}\\hat{\\jmath} + \\frac{dv_z}{dt}\\hat{k}$",
      "Directional vs magnitude acceleration: acceleration is non-zero whenever velocity magnitude changes, direction changes, or both change"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "title": "Projectile Motion: Decoupled Kinematics and Parabolic Trajectories",
    "scope": "Analyzes two-dimensional motion under constant downward gravitational acceleration without air resistance. Formulates the total motion as two completely independent one-dimensional motions: unaccelerated horizontal motion and uniformly accelerated vertical free fall. Derives the algebraic equation of the parabolic trajectory, the horizontal range formula, and the time-of-flight ratio for complementary launch angles.",
    "key_points": [
      "Independence of orthogonal motions: $a_x = 0$ and $a_y = -g$",
      "Parametric equations: $x(t) = x_0 + (v_0\\cos\\theta_0)t$ and $y(t) = y_0 + (v_0\\sin\\theta_0)t - \\frac{1}{2}gt^2$",
      "Trajectory equation: $y(x) = (\\tan\\theta_0)x - \\frac{g x^2}{2(v_0\\cos\\theta_0)^2}$, demonstrating a parabolic path $y = ax + bx^2$",
      "Horizontal range: $R = \\frac{v_0^2}{g}\\sin 2\\theta_0$, reaching maximum at $\\theta_0 = 45^\\circ$",
      "Complementary launch angles ($\theta$ and $90^\\circ - \\theta$) yield identical ranges $R(\\theta_1) = R(\\theta_2)$ with distinct flight times $t_{\\text{flight}} = \\frac{2v_0\\sin\\theta_0}{g}$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "title": "Uniform Circular Motion and Centripetal Acceleration",
    "scope": "Investigates circular motion at constant speed, explaining why constant speed entails non-zero acceleration due to continuously turning velocity vectors. Presents the period of revolution, centripetal acceleration magnitude, and its strictly inward radial direction. Details the full analytical derivation of centripetal acceleration using Cartesian coordinate components and time differentiation, alongside physiological high-g limits.",
    "key_points": [
      "Period of revolution: $T = \\frac{2\\pi r}{v}$ and constant speed $v = \\frac{2\\pi r}{T}$",
      "Centripetal acceleration magnitude: $a = \\frac{v^2}{r} = \\frac{2\\pi v}{T}$ directed radially toward the center",
      "Coordinate derivation: $\\vec{v} = (-v\\sin\\theta)\\hat{\\imath} + (v\\cos\\theta)\\hat{\\jmath} = \\left(-v\\frac{y_p}{r}\\right)\\hat{\\imath} + \\left(v\\frac{x_p}{r}\\right)\\hat{\\jmath}$",
      "Time derivative: $\\vec{a} = \\frac{d\\vec{v}}{dt} = \\left(-\\frac{v^2}{r}\\cos\\theta\\right)\\hat{\\imath} + \\left(-\\frac{v^2}{r}\\sin\\theta\\right)\\hat{\\jmath}$, giving $|\vec{a}| = \\frac{v^2}{r}$ and angle $\\phi = \\theta$ pointing to the origin",
      "Physiological centripetal effects: g-LOC, tunnel vision at $\\sim 4g$, and reversing turn kinematic calculation where $\\vec{v}_f = -\\vec{v}_i$ implies a half-period"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "title": "Intrinsic Coordinates: Tangential and Normal Accelerations",
    "scope": "Develops the natural (intrinsic) coordinate framework for arbitrary curved paths using unit tangent and normal vectors. Derives the decomposition of the total acceleration vector into tangential acceleration (rate of speed change) and normal acceleration (rate of direction change). Proves the geometric proportion relating the change of the unit tangent vector to the local radius of curvature.",
    "key_points": [
      "Velocity in intrinsic coordinates: $\\vec{v}(t) = v(t)\\boldsymbol{\\tau}(t)$, where speed $v = \\frac{dl}{dt}$ and $\\boldsymbol{\\tau}$ is the unit tangent vector",
      "Acceleration decomposition: $\\vec{a} = \\frac{d\\vec{v}}{dt} = \\frac{dv}{dt}\\boldsymbol{\\tau} + v\\frac{d\\boldsymbol{\\tau}}{dt} = \\vec{a}_\\tau + \\vec{a}_n$",
      "Tangential acceleration: $\\vec{a}_\\tau = \\frac{dv}{dt}\\boldsymbol{\\tau} = a_\\tau\\boldsymbol{\\tau}$, governing changes in speed magnitude",
      "Normal acceleration derivation: $\\frac{d\\boldsymbol{\\tau}}{dt} = v\\frac{d\\boldsymbol{\\tau}}{dl}$; by similar triangles $\\frac{|d\\boldsymbol{\\tau}|}{\\tau} = \\frac{dl}{\\rho}$ with $\\tau=1$, yielding $\\frac{d\\tau}{dl} = \\frac{1}{\\rho}$",
      "Normal acceleration vector: $\\vec{a}_n = \\frac{v^2}{\\rho}\\boldsymbol{n}$, directed along the principal normal toward the center of curvature, with total acceleration $a = \\sqrt{a_\\tau^2 + a_n^2}$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "title": "Curvature, Radius of Curvature, and Vector Projections",
    "scope": "Provides algebraic and vector formulas for computing tangential acceleration, normal acceleration, curvature, and radius of curvature directly from Cartesian components. Demonstrates how to project acceleration onto velocity via dot products and cross products without needing intrinsic angles. Teaches the complete method for determining the explicit path equation and position-dependent radius of curvature for given velocity fields.",
    "key_points": [
      "Tangential acceleration vector via dot product: $\\vec{a}_\\tau = \\frac{(\\vec{a}\\cdot\\vec{v})}{(\\vec{v}\\cdot\\vec{v})}\\vec{v} = \\frac{a_x v_x + a_y v_y}{v_x^2 + v_y^2}(v_x\\hat{\\imath} + v_y\\hat{\\jmath})$ with scalar value $a_\\tau = \\frac{\\vec{a}\\cdot\\vec{v}}{v}$",
      "Normal acceleration vector: $\\vec{a}_n = \\vec{a} - \\vec{a}_\\tau = \\frac{a_x v_y - a_y v_x}{v_x^2 + v_y^2}(v_y\\hat{\\imath} - v_x\\hat{\\jmath})$ with scalar value $a_n = \\frac{|a_x v_y - a_y v_x|}{v}$",
      "Curvature $\\rho$ and radius of curvature $R$: $\\rho = \\frac{1}{R} = \\frac{a_n}{v^2} = \\frac{|\\vec{a}\\times\\vec{v}|}{v^3} = \\frac{|a_x v_y - a_y v_x|}{v^3}$",
      "Radius of curvature formula: $R = \\frac{v^3}{|a_x v_y - a_y v_x|} = \\frac{(v_x^2 + v_y^2)^{3/2}}{|a_x v_y - a_y v_x|}$",
      "Trajectory and curvature derivation method: integrating $v_x(t), v_y(t)$ to eliminate $t$ for $y(x)$, computing $\\vec{a} = d\\vec{v}/dt$, and evaluating $R(x)$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "title": "Pursuit Kinematics: Symmetric Multi-Agent and Moving Target Pursuit",
    "scope": "Examines pursuit problems where pursuers continuously orient their instantaneous velocity vectors toward a moving target. Covers symmetric convergence in equilateral multi-agent systems via relative velocity projection along moving edges. Formulates the differential equations for perpendicular pursuer-target tracking and derives the exact analytical convergence time using dual projections along the line of sight and target trajectory.",
    "key_points": [
      "Pursuit condition: pursuer velocity $\\vec{v}_A$ is continually collinear with line-of-sight unit vector $\\boldsymbol{\\tau}_{AB} = \\frac{\\vec{r}_B - \\vec{r}_A}{|\\vec{r}_B - \\vec{r}_A|}$",
      "Equilateral triangle pursuit: closing speed along each side $-\\frac{dl}{dt} = v_1 + v_{2,\\parallel} = v + v\\cos(\\pi/3) = \\frac{3}{2}v$, yielding convergence time $t = \\frac{2a}{3v}$",
      "System of ODEs for tracking a rectilinear target ($X_B(t) = ut, Y_B = 0$): $\\frac{dX_A}{dt} = v\\frac{X_B - X_A}{\\sqrt{(X_B - X_A)^2 + Y_A^2}}$ and $\\frac{dY_A}{dt} = -\\sqrt{v^2 - (dX_A/dt)^2}$",
      "Line-of-sight closing integral: $l = \\int_0^T (v - u\\cos\\alpha(t))dt = vT - u\\int_0^T \\cos\\alpha(t)dt$",
      "Transverse coordinate matching: $uT = \\int_0^T v\\cos\\alpha(t)dt \\implies \\int_0^T \\cos\\alpha(t)dt = \\frac{uT}{v}$, yielding closed-form convergence time $T = \\frac{vl}{v^2 - u^2}$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "title": "Kinematic Reconstruction and Relative Motion Analysis",
    "scope": "Synthesizes advanced problem-solving techniques for reconstructing trajectories and frames of reference from partial kinematic boundary data. Covers velocity reconstruction from piecewise-constant acceleration via integration. Teaches 1D pursuit gap reduction, relative wind speed algebraic solution in round-trip transit, and geometric reconstruction of a circular orbit's center and radius from two velocity and acceleration state snapshots.",
    "key_points": [
      "Piecewise velocity reconstruction: $v(t) = v(0) + \\int_0^t a(t')dt'$ as the area under the acceleration graph",
      "One-dimensional pursuit time: $t = \\frac{S_{\\text{lead}}}{v_{\\text{pursuer}} - v_{\\text{target}}}$",
      "Relative velocity in headwind/tailwind round trips: $\\frac{S}{V - V_0} - \\Delta t = \\frac{S}{V + V_0} \\implies V = \\sqrt{V_0(2S + V_0)}$",
      "Average speed kinematic relation under constant acceleration: $S = v_0 t + \\frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $a = \\frac{v_1 - v_0}{t}$ yields $v_0 = \\frac{2S - v_1 t}{t}$",
      "Circular trajectory reconstruction from states: interpreting orthogonal velocity and inward centripetal acceleration directions to identify quadrant traversal, determining arc fraction $\\Delta s = \\frac{3}{4}(2\\pi R) = v(t_2 - t_1)$, and locating the circle center $[x_0 + R, y_0]$"
    ]
  }
]
